"""Schema inference and validation for JSON record streams."""

from .core import Lens, SchemaConflict

__all__ = ["Lens", "SchemaConflict"]
__version__ = "0.3.0"

content.content:
1	"""Core schema inference and validation logic.
2	
3	A schema is a tree of nodes. Object nodes carry a mapping of field name to
4	field entry; each field entry records the set of observed types, how many
5	records carried the field, how many records were seen at that level, and
6	whether the field is optional. Array nodes merge their element types.
7	
8	Inference is a streaming fold: records are folded one at a time and never
9	retained, so peak memory tracks the size of the statistics tree, not the
10	number of records. The tree itself can be bounded with two resource limits
11	given to ``Lens``: ``max_fields`` caps how many field entries one object
12	node tracks exactly (further distinct names fold into a shared overflow
13	entry kept under the node's ``"overflow"`` key), and ``max_depth`` caps how
14	deep object and array nodes are tracked (deeper subtrees collapse into
15	summary nodes that keep only counts and element kinds). Every statistic
16	that has been approximated is flagged with ``"approximate": true`` in the
17	schema tree and listed under the ``"approximate"`` key of ``Lens.stats``,
18	so precision loss is always visible and never silent. With no limits (the
19	default) no approximation is ever triggered and the folded schema is
20	exactly the schema produced by folding every record in one pass. The field
21	cap is also enforced after two batches are merged, so a merged object node
22	can never hold more exact field entries than the cap even when the two
23	batches named disjoint sets; the excess entries fold into that node's
24	overflow entry.
25	
26	Persistence is multi-revision, incremental and crash safe. Each ``save``
27	is a commit serialized through a lock file inside the lens directory: it
28	folds the records folded since the last load or save into the schema of
29	the newest committed revision and writes the result as one brand new,
30	complete revision file in the ``versions`` directory, each revision
31	carrying its own monotonic number and checksum. Revision files are never
32	rewritten; a new revision only appears by an atomic rename of a fully
33	synced file and its number is one greater than the previous newest, so
34	readers see a total order and old revisions are pruned once more than
35	``max_versions`` complete revisions exist. A crash or an interrupted
36	commit can therefore only ever leave complete revisions, and any reader
37	observes either the previous complete revision or the next one, never a
38	half-written schema. A revision is
39	parsed, structurally validated and checksummed completely before any of
40	its content is handed out; a missing or corrupt requested revision raises
41	``SchemaConflict`` and leaves every other revision usable.
42	
43	``check`` and ``schema`` can either target an explicit revision number or
44	read the snapshot the lens was opened (``load``-ed) at; inference keeps
45	appending batches as before. ``versions`` lists the committed revisions
46	oldest first and ``rollback`` expresses the target revision's schema as a
47	brand new commit, so history is appended to and never rewritten. A
48	revision that has already been pruned (or never existed) makes a rollback
49	raise ``SchemaConflict`` without touching any committed revision.
50	
51	A lens directory holding only the old single-file format (``schema.json``)
52	is still read; the legacy file is migrated in place into the revisions
53	layout on first read, and a failed migration leaves the original file and
54	the in-memory schema untouched and raises ``SchemaConflict`` so it can be
55	retried later.
56	
57	The oldest segment of the history can be compacted into one baseline
58	version. A baseline file carries the schema and statistics exactly as they
59	stood at the end of the merged range (the folded tree is checked
60	field-for-field against the last merged revision before the switch), and a
61	small manifest in the versions directory is the single pointer naming at
62	most one baseline file. Compaction stages a temp artifact, validates it
63	fully, only then atomically replaces the manifest, and deletes no merged
64	input until that switch has landed; a crash mid-compaction is reconciled
65	into "completely happened" or "never happened" the next time the lock is
66	taken. Reads never wait on a compaction: while it runs they route through
67	the old manifest to complete revisions, and afterwards the baseline is
68	readable as its anchor revision while the revisions merged into it answer
69	``SchemaConflict``.
70	
71	``compat(old, new)`` reads two committed snapshots without changing memory
72	or any revision and reports how the evolution between them affects the
73	records each side accepts. One symmetric tree diff derives both directions
74	at once, judged by the same rules ``check`` enforces: ``backward`` says
75	whether the new revision still accepts records legal under the old one,
76	``forward`` the reverse. Adding an optional field, relaxing a required
77	field or widening a type set is non-breaking in the direction that accepts;
78	removing a field, tightening optionality, narrowing a type set or dropping
79	a nested type branch is breaking there. A branch either side only describes
80	approximately (an overflow entry, an approximate field entry, or a
81	depth-capped subtree) cannot be settled and makes both directions
82	``unknown``, listing its source in ``unknown_reasons`` with the same paths
83	``stats`` uses; a revision compared with itself is compatible in both
84	directions with no changes.
85	"""
86	
87	from __future__ import annotations
88	
89	import contextlib
90	import copy
91	import hashlib
92	import itertools
93	import json
94	import os
95	import threading
96	import time
97	from pathlib import Path
98	from typing import Any, Iterable, Iterator
99	
100	try:
101	    import fcntl
102	except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - Windows
103	    fcntl = None  # type: ignore[assignment]
104	try:
105	    import msvcrt
106	except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - Windows
107	    msvcrt = None  # type: ignore[assignment]
108	
109	SCHEMA_FILENAME = "schema.json"
110	LOCK_FILENAME = "schema.lock"
111	VERSIONS_DIRNAME = "versions"
112	REVISION_PREFIX = "revision-"
113	REVISION_SUFFIX = ".json"
114	BASELINE_PREFIX = "baseline-"
115	BASELINE_SUFFIX = ".json"
116	MANIFEST_FILENAME = "manifest.json"
117	DEFAULT_MAX_VERSIONS = 10
118	DEFAULT_COMPACT_KEEP = 5
119	SCHEMA_VERSION = 3
120	# Version 1 files predate approximation markers; version 2 is the single
121	# file layout. All three encodings carry the same node tree, so legacy
122	# files migrate to the revisions layout without re-interpreting the tree.
123	READABLE_VERSIONS = (1, 2, SCHEMA_VERSION)
124	# The overflow entry marks approximated locations in stats paths. It is a
125	# key no JSON object can literally carry, so it can never collide with a
126	# real field name (a field literally named "*" stays locatable as
127	# ``$["*"]`` while the marker renders as ``$.*``).
128	OVERFLOW_MARKER = "*\x00*"
129	
130	# Each compaction attempt stages its artifact under a unique temp name;
131	# the file only takes its final baseline name by an atomic rename taken
132	# under the commit lock, so concurrent compactions never overwrite each
133	# other's staging file and a retried switch can never unlink a baseline a
134	# winning switch already committed.
135	_STAGING_COUNTER = itertools.count()
136	
137	
138	def _staging_name() -> str:
139	    return f"staging-{os.getpid()}-{next(_STAGING_COUNTER)}.tmp"
140	
141	
142	def _write_staging(directory: Path, text: str) -> Path:
143	    """Write a uniquely named, fully synced staging file in ``directory``."""
144	    for _ in range(100):
145	        path = directory / _staging_name()
146	        try:
147	            fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o644)
148	        except FileExistsError:
149	            continue
150	        try:
151	            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
152	                handle.write(text)
153	                handle.flush()
154	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
155	        except BaseException:
156	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
157	                os.unlink(path)
158	            raise
159	        return path
160	    raise SchemaConflict("cannot allocate a compaction staging file")
161	
162	_KINDS = ("null", "boolean", "number", "string", "array", "object")
163	
164	
165	class SchemaConflict(Exception):
166	    """Raised when an operation conflicts with the stored schema state."""
167	
168	
169	class _RevisionMissing(SchemaConflict):
170	    """Internal: a mapped revision/baseline file is not on disk (a race)."""
171	
172	
173	def _kind_of(value: Any) -> str:
174	    if value is None:
175	        return "null"
176	    if isinstance(value, bool):
177	        return "boolean"
178	    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
179	        return "number"
180	    if isinstance(value, str):
181	        return "string"
182	    if isinstance(value, list):
183	        return "array"
184	    if isinstance(value, dict):
185	        return "object"
186	    raise ValueError(f"unsupported value type: {type(value).__name__}")
187	
188	
189	def _new_node(kind: str) -> dict:
190	    node: dict[str, Any] = {"kind": kind}
191	    if kind == "object":
192	        node["fields"] = {}
193	        node["count"] = 0
194	    elif kind == "array":
195	        node["elements"] = {}
196	    return node
197	
198	
199	def _collapsed_node(kind: str) -> dict:
200	    """A depth-capped node: marked approximate, sub-structure not tracked.
201	
202	    Collapsed objects keep only a record count; collapsed arrays keep only
203	    the kinds of their elements (each of which is itself collapsed or a
204	    scalar), so the memory a collapsed subtree can use is bounded.
205	    """
206	    node: dict[str, Any] = {"kind": kind, "approximate": True}
207	    if kind == "object":
208	        node["count"] = 0
209	    elif kind == "array":
210	        node["elements"] = {}
211	    return node
212	
213	
214	def _is_collapsed(node: dict) -> bool:
215	    """Whether an object node is a depth-capped summary without fields."""
216	    return (
217	        node["kind"] == "object"
218	        and bool(node.get("approximate"))
219	        and "fields" not in node
220	    )
221	
222	
223	def _new_field() -> dict:
224	    return {"types": {}, "observed": 0, "total": 0, "optional": False}
225	
226	
227	def _overflow_add_name(entry: dict, name: str) -> None:
228	    """Record that ``name`` really folded into an overflow entry.
229	
230	    The list is kept sorted (and de-duplicated) so the schema tree stays
231	    canonical across folds, commits and reloads. An explicit ``names:
232	    None`` marks a pre-tracking overflow entry whose provenance is
233	    unknown; adding a known name cannot narrow that, so it stays unknown.
234	    """
235	    if "names" in entry and entry["names"] is None:
236	        return
237	    names = entry.setdefault("names", [])
238	    if name not in names:
239	        names.append(name)
240	        names.sort()
241	
242	
243	def _union_overflow_names(left: dict | None, right: dict | None) -> list[str] | None:
244	    """Union the folded-name provenance of two entries.
245	
246	    A normal exact entry carries no ``names`` key (empty provenance); an
247	    explicit ``names: None`` marks an overflow entry loaded from a file
248	    written before provenance was tracked, whose folded names are unknown
249	    and must keep widening for every name.

251	    if left is None or right is None:
252	        return None
253

255	        if "names" not in entry:
256	            return []
257	        return entry["names"]

259	    ln = provenance(left)
260	    rn = provenance(right)

266	def _fold_object(
267	    node: dict,
268	    record: dict,
269	    depth: int = 0,
270	    max_fields: int | None = None,
271	    max_depth: int | None = None,
272	) -> None:
273	    if _is_collapsed(node):
274	        node["count"] += 1
275	        return
276	    node["count"] += 1
277	    fields = node["fields"]
278	    overflow = node.get("overflow")
279	    for name, value in record.items():
280	        entry = fields.get(name)
281	        if entry is None:
282	            if max_fields is not None and len(fields) >= max_fields:
283	                # The field cap is reached: fold this and every further new
284	                # name into the shared overflow entry. The entry is marked
285	                # approximate; its type set only widens and its observation
286	                # count only grows, exactly like an exact entry's.
287	                if overflow is None:
288	                    overflow = _new_field()
289	                    overflow["approximate"] = True
290	                    node["overflow"] = overflow
291	                _overflow_add_name(overflow, name)
292	                overflow["observed"] += 1
293	                _fold_value(overflow["types"], value, depth + 1, max_fields, max_depth)
294	                continue
295	            entry = _new_field()
296	            fields[name] = entry
297	        entry["observed"] += 1
298	        _fold_value(entry["types"], value, depth + 1, max_fields, max_depth)

306	    max_depth: int | None = None,
307	) -> None:
308	    kind = _kind_of(value)
309	    node = types.get(kind)
310	    if node is None:
311	        if max_depth is not None and kind in ("object", "array") and depth > max_depth:
312	            node = _collapsed_node(kind)
313	        else:
314	            node = _new_node(kind)
315	        types[kind] = node
316	    if kind == "object":
317	        _fold_object(node, value, depth, max_fields, max_depth)
318	    elif kind == "array":

344	def _cap_object_fields(node: dict, max_fields: int | None) -> None:
345	    """Fold exact fields beyond the cap into the overflow entry.
346	
347	    Applied recursively after two batches merge: folding each batch under
348	    the cap bounds the names it introduces, but disjoint names across
349	    batches could otherwise leave a merged node with up to twice the cap
350	    exact entries. Entries are folded in name order, so which names stay
351	    exact is deterministic; folded entries widen the existing overflow
352	    entry (which may itself carry records seen under names neither batch
353	    tracked exactly) and the result is marked approximate.
354	    """
355	    if _is_collapsed(node):
356	        return
357	    if max_fields is not None and len(node["fields"]) > max_fields:
358	        # Keep the first names tracked exactly and fold the rest; merged
359	        # field order follows global first-seen order (left batch then
360	        # names new in the right batch), so this lands on exactly the
361	        # entries a single capped pass over every record would have kept.
362	        names = list(node["fields"])
363	        excess = names[max_fields:]
364	        fields = node["fields"]
365	        overflow = node.get("overflow")
366	        for name in excess:
367	            entry = fields.pop(name)
368	            overflow = (
369	                _merge_field(overflow, entry)
370	                if overflow is not None
371	                else copy.deepcopy(entry)
372	            )
373	            # The popped entry was an exact field at this node; its name is
374	            # the provenance it adds to the node's overflow. Overflow
375	            # provenance deeper in its type tree rides along in the merge.
376	            _overflow_add_name(overflow, name)
377	            overflow["approximate"] = True
378	            node["overflow"] = overflow
379	    for entry in node["fields"].values():
380	        for child in entry["types"].values():
381	            _cap_node_fields(child, max_fields)
382	    overflow = node.get("overflow")
383	    if overflow is not None:
384	        for child in overflow["types"].values():
385	            _cap_node_fields(child, max_fields)
386

388	def _cap_node_fields(node: dict, max_fields: int | None) -> None:
389	    if node["kind"] == "object":
390	        _cap_object_fields(node, max_fields)
391	    elif node["kind"] == "array":
392	        for child in node["elements"].values():
393	            _cap_node_fields(child, max_fields)

396	def _merge_node(left: dict, right: dict) -> dict:
397	    """Fold two schema nodes over disjoint batches into one new node."""
398	    kind = left["kind"]
399	    if kind == "object":
400	        if _is_collapsed(left) or _is_collapsed(right):
401	            # One side gave up per-field detail, so the union can only be
402	            # reported as a collapsed, marked summary.
403	            node = _collapsed_node("object")
404	            node["count"] = left["count"] + right["count"]
405	            return node
406	        node = _new_node("object")
407	        node["count"] = left["count"] + right["count"]
408	        left_overflow = left.get("overflow")
409	        right_overflow = right.get("overflow")
410	        names = list(left["fields"]) + [
411	            name for name in right["fields"] if name not in left["fields"]
412	        ]
413	        for name in names:
414	            le = left["fields"].get(name)
415	            re = right["fields"].get(name)
416	            if le is None:
417	                # The field is missing on the left; if the left capped its
418	                # fields, its occurrences of this field landed in the left
419	                # overflow entry, so the merged entry must absorb them and
420	                # be marked approximate. That field's own occurrences on
421	                # the right prove its name is folded too.
422	                if left_overflow is not None:
423	                    entry = _merge_field(left_overflow, re)
424	                    _overflow_add_name(entry, name)
425	                    entry["approximate"] = True
426	                else:
427	                    entry = copy.deepcopy(re)
428	            elif re is None:
429	                if right_overflow is not None:
430	                    entry = _merge_field(le, right_overflow)
431	                    _overflow_add_name(entry, name)
432	                    entry["approximate"] = True
433	                else:
434	                    entry = copy.deepcopy(le)
435	            else:
436	                entry = _merge_field(le, re)
437	            node["fields"][name] = entry
438	        if left_overflow is not None or right_overflow is not None:
439	            if left_overflow is None:
440	                overflow = copy.deepcopy(right_overflow)
441	            elif right_overflow is None:
442	                overflow = copy.deepcopy(left_overflow)
443	            else:
444	                overflow = _merge_field(left_overflow, right_overflow)
445	            overflow["approximate"] = True
446	            node["overflow"] = overflow
447	        return node
448	    if kind == "array":
449	        node = _new_node("array")
450	        if left.get("approximate") or right.get("approximate"):
451	            node["approximate"] = True
452	        kinds = list(left["elements"]) + [
453	            element_kind
454	            for element_kind in right["elements"]
455	            if element_kind not in left["elements"]
456	        ]
457	        for element_kind in kinds:
458	            lc = left["elements"].get(element_kind)
459	            rc = right["elements"].get(element_kind)
460	            if lc is None:
461	                node["elements"][element_kind] = copy.deepcopy(rc)
462	            elif rc is None:
463	                node["elements"][element_kind] = copy.deepcopy(lc)
464	            else:
465	                node["elements"][element_kind] = _merge_node(lc, rc)
466	        return node
467	    return _new_node(kind)

497	    """Return the part of ``mem`` folded after ``base`` was taken."""
498	    kind = mem["kind"]
499	    if kind == "object":
500	        if _is_collapsed(mem):

502	            node["count"] = mem["count"] - base.get("count", 0)

506	        base_fields = base.get("fields") or {}
507	        for name, entry in mem["fields"].items():
508	            base_entry = base_fields.get(name)

510	                node["fields"][name] = copy.deepcopy(entry)
511	            else:
512	                node["fields"][name] = _subtract_field(entry, base_entry)
513	        mem_overflow = mem.get("overflow")
514	        if mem_overflow is not None:
515	            base_overflow = base.get("overflow")
516	            if base_overflow is None:
517	                node["overflow"] = copy.deepcopy(mem_overflow)
518	            else:
519	                node["overflow"] = _subtract_field(mem_overflow, base_overflow)
520	        return node
521	    if kind == "array":
522	        node = _new_node("array")
523	        if mem.get("approximate"):
524	            node["approximate"] = True

526	        for element_kind, child in mem["elements"].items():
527	            base_child = base_elements.get(element_kind)
528	            if base_child is None:
529	                node["elements"][element_kind] = copy.deepcopy(child)
530	            else:

536	def _subtract_field(mem: dict, base: dict) -> dict:
537	    entry = _new_field()

539	    if mem.get("approximate"):
540	        entry["approximate"] = True

542	    if mem_names is not None:
543	        # The delta cannot attribute provenance per name (only aggregate
544	        # counts are kept), so it carries every name its memory ever folded

546	        # only ever widens validation for genuinely folded names.

549	        base_child = base["types"].get(kind)
550	        if base_child is None:
551	            entry["types"][kind] = copy.deepcopy(child)
552	        else:
553	            entry["types"][kind] = _subtract_node(child, base_child)
554	    return entry

558	    # An identifier is joined with a dot; every other key is quoted in
559	    # brackets so a name containing a dot or a backslash can never be read
560	    # as a path separator: $["a.b"] is distinct from $.a.b.
561	    if name.isidentifier():

563	    return f"{path}[{json.dumps(name)}]"

570	    ``.*`` segment cannot be produced by ``_join`` for any real field name;

576	def _check_object(node: dict, record: dict, path: str, reports: list[str]) -> None:
577	    if _is_collapsed(node):
578	        # A depth-capped node tracked no fields, so nothing inside the
579	        # record's value can be checked; the approximation is marked in
580	        # the schema instead of guessed about here.
581	        return
582	    fields = node["fields"]
583	    overflow = node.get("overflow")
584	    overflow_names = None if overflow is None else overflow.get("names")
585	    for name in record:
586	        if name not in fields:
587	            if overflow is not None and (
588	                overflow_names is None or name in overflow_names
589	            ):
590	                # Only names that really folded into the overflow entry are
591	                # checked against its widened type set; ``names is None``
592	                # marks a legacy overflow entry with unknown provenance. A
593	                # name never seen before is still unexpected.
594	                _check_value(overflow["types"], record[name], _join(path, name), reports)
595	            else:
596	                reports.append(f"{_join(path, name)}: unexpected field")
597	    for name, entry in fields.items():
598	        if name not in record:
599	            if not entry["optional"]:
600	                reports.append(f"{_join(path, name)}: missing required field")
601	            continue
602	        _check_value(entry["types"], record[name], _join(path, name), reports)

606	    kind = _kind_of(value)

609	        expected = ", ".join(sorted(types))
610	        reports.append(f"{path}: type {kind} not in field types [{expected}]")
611	        return
612	    if kind == "object":
613	        _check_object(node, value, path, reports)
614	    elif kind == "array":

619	# -- cross-revision compatibility -------------------------------------------
620	#
621	# Compatibility is read straight off the two committed schema trees, using
622	# exactly what ``check`` decides with: a record is accepted when every
623	# field it carries is a known (or genuinely overflow-folded) field whose
624	# value kind is in the entry's type set, every required field is present,
625	# and nested branches recurse. One symmetric walk therefore derives both
626	# directions at once: ``backward`` asks whether the new tree accepts every
627	# record the old tree accepts, ``forward`` the reverse.
628	#
629	# Each branch returns a ``(backward, forward)`` verdict pair. A branch
630	# either tree can only describe approximately - an overflow entry that may
631	# route the field, an entry flagged approximate, or a depth-capped subtree
632	# - is unknown in both directions and lists its source, in the same paths
633	# ``stats`` uses for approximated statistics (``$.*`` for an overflow
634	# entry, the subtree's own path for a collapsed node). The one exception
635	# is comparing a revision with itself: that revision is known to accept its
636	# own records, so ``Lens.compat`` answers compatible in both directions
637	# with no reasons after the revision has been read and validated.
638	
639	_COMPATIBLE = "compatible"
640	_BREAKING = "breaking"
641	_UNKNOWN = "unknown"
642	
643	
644	def _combine_pair(pair: tuple[str, str], other: tuple[str, str]) -> tuple[str, str]:
645	    return (_worst(pair[0], other[0]), _worst(pair[1], other[1]))
646

648	def _worst(left: str, right: str) -> str:
649	    """Aggregate branch verdicts for one direction.
650	
651	    A branch that demonstrably rejects a legal record settles the
652	    direction as breaking even when another branch is unknowable; without
653	    one of those an unknown branch degrades it to unknown.
654	    """
655	    if left == _BREAKING or right == _BREAKING:
656	        return _BREAKING
657	    if left == _UNKNOWN or right == _UNKNOWN:
658	        return _UNKNOWN
659	    return _COMPATIBLE

662	def _overflow_live(entry: dict) -> bool:
663	    """Whether an overflow entry can route a field name during check.
664	
665	    An entry with known but empty provenance routes nothing; an explicit
666	    ``names: None`` (a pre-tracking overflow entry) routes any name.
667	    """
668	    names = entry.get("names", [])
669	    return names is None or bool(names)

672	def _overflow_routes(entry: dict | None, name: str) -> bool:
673	    if entry is None or not _overflow_live(entry):
674	        return False
675	    names = entry.get("names")
676	    return names is None or name in names

679	class _CompatDiffer:
680	    """Symmetric diff of two validated snapshots, aligned with ``check``."""
681	
682	    def __init__(self) -> None:
683	        self.changes: list[dict] = []
684	        self.reasons: set[str] = set()
685	
686	    def diff(self, old_root: dict, new_root: dict) -> dict:
687	        backward, forward = self.compare_object(old_root, new_root, "$")
688	        self.changes.sort(key=lambda change: (change["path"], change["change"]))
689	        return {
690	            "backward": backward,
691	            "forward": forward,
692	            "changes": self.changes,
693	            "unknown_reasons": sorted(self.reasons),
694	        }
695	
696	    def change(self, path: str, category: str, breaking: bool) -> None:
697	        self.changes.append(
698	            {"path": path, "change": category, "breaking": breaking}
699	        )

701	    def compare_object(self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
702	        if _is_collapsed(old) or _is_collapsed(new):
703	            # A depth-capped object lets anything nested through check, so
704	            # neither direction can be settled field by field.
705	            self.reasons.add(path)
706	            return _UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN
707	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
708	        old_fields = old["fields"]
709	        new_fields = new["fields"]
710	        old_overflow = old.get("overflow")
711	        new_overflow = new.get("overflow")
712	        for name in sorted(set(old_fields) | set(new_fields)):
713	            field_path = _join(path, name)
714	            old_entry = old_fields.get(name)
715	            new_entry = new_fields.get(name)
716	            if old_entry is not None and new_entry is not None:
717	                verdict = _combine_pair(
718	                    verdict, self.compare_entry(old_entry, new_entry, field_path)
719	                )
720	            elif old_entry is not None:
721	                # The field disappears from the new exact fields. New check
722	                # only accepts it when the name really folded into the new
723	                # overflow entry, whose merged type set is approximate.
724	                if _overflow_routes(new_overflow, name):
725	                    self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
726	                    verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
727	                else:
728	                    # New check rejects records carrying it; old records
729	                    # omitting it additionally fail an old required field
730	                    # under the forward direction.
731	                    self.change(field_path, "field_removed", True)
732	                    verdict = _combine_pair(
733	                        verdict,
734	                        (_BREAKING,
735	                         _BREAKING if not old_entry["optional"] else _COMPATIBLE),
736	                    )
737	            else:
738	                # The field appears only among the new exact fields. Old
739	                # check accepts it only through its own overflow entry.
740	                if _overflow_routes(old_overflow, name):
741	                    self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
742	                    verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
743	                else:
744	                    # Backward: an old record omits it, so a new required
745	                    # field rejects that record while a new optional one
746	                    # lets it through. Forward: old check calls any record
747	                    # carrying it unexpected.
748	                    self.change(
749	                        field_path, "field_added", not new_entry["optional"]
750	                    )
751	                    verdict = _combine_pair(
752	                        verdict,
753	                        (_BREAKING if not new_entry["optional"] else _COMPATIBLE,
754	                         _BREAKING),
755	                    )
756	        # A live overflow entry on either side folds names whose accepted
757	        # branches cannot be attributed exactly; every branch it governs is
758	        # unknown both ways. The marker can never be a real field name.
759	        for entry in (old_overflow, new_overflow):
760	            if entry is not None and _overflow_live(entry):
761	                self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
762	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
763	        return verdict

765	    def compare_entry(
766	        self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str
767	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
768	        if old.get("approximate") or new.get("approximate"):
769	            # An entry flagged approximate absorbed overflow statistics in
770	            # an exact field position; its accepted value set cannot be
771	            # attributed precisely, so no change beneath it is asserted.
772	            self.reasons.add(path)
773	            return _UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN
774	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
775	        if old["optional"] != new["optional"]:
776	            if old["optional"]:
777	                # Optional becomes required: old records may omit it.
778	                self.change(path, "optional_to_required", True)
779	                verdict = (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE)
780	            else:
781	                # Required becomes optional: new records may omit it.
782	                self.change(path, "required_to_optional", False)
783	                verdict = (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING)
784	        verdict = _combine_pair(
785	            verdict, self.compare_types(old["types"], new["types"], path, "type")
786	        )

789	    def compare_types(
790	        self, old_types: dict, new_types: dict, path: str, prefix: str
791	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
792	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
793	        for kind in _KINDS:
794	            if kind not in old_types and kind not in new_types:
795	                continue
796	            old_node = old_types.get(kind)
797	            new_node = new_types.get(kind)
798	            if old_node is not None and new_node is not None:
799	                verdict = _combine_pair(
800	                    verdict, self.compare_kind(old_node, new_node, path)
801	                )
802	            elif old_node is not None:
803	                # Records of this kind are legal on the old side but the
804	                # new type set no longer contains it (narrowing).
805	                self.change(path, f"{prefix}_{kind}_removed", True)
806	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE))
807	            else:
808	                # The new side widened with this kind; old check rejects
809	                # new records that take it (forward breaking), while old
810	                # records still pass the new, wider check.
811	                self.change(path, f"{prefix}_{kind}_added", False)
812	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING))

815	    def compare_kind(
816	        self, old_node: dict, new_node: dict, path: str

843	            new_child = new["elements"].get(kind)

1216	    statistic exact and the folded schema identical to folding all records
1217	    in one pass. Records themselves are never retained, so peak memory
1218	    tracks these limits rather than the number of records folded.

"""Core schema inference and validation logic.

A schema is a tree of nodes. Object nodes carry a mapping of field name to
field entry; each field entry records the set of observed types, how many
records carried the field, how many records were seen at that level, and
whether the field is optional. Array nodes merge their element types.

Inference is a streaming fold: records are folded one at a time and never
retained, so peak memory tracks the size of the statistics tree, not the
number of records. The tree itself can be bounded with two resource limits
given to ``Lens``: ``max_fields`` caps how many field entries one object
node tracks exactly (further distinct names fold into a shared overflow
entry kept under the node's ``"overflow"`` key), and ``max_depth`` caps how
deep object and array nodes are tracked (deeper subtrees collapse into
summary nodes that keep only counts and element kinds). Every statistic
that has been approximated is flagged with ``"approximate": true`` in the
schema tree and listed under the ``"approximate"`` key of ``Lens.stats``,
so precision loss is always visible and never silent. With no limits (the
default) no approximation is ever triggered and the folded schema is
exactly the schema produced by folding every record in one pass. The field
cap is also enforced after two batches are merged, so a merged object node
can never hold more exact field entries than the cap even when the two
batches named disjoint sets; the excess entries fold into that node's
overflow entry.

Persistence is multi-revision, incremental and crash safe. Each ``save``
is a commit serialized through a lock file inside the lens directory: it
folds the records folded since the last load or save into the schema of
the newest committed revision and writes the result as one brand new,
complete revision file in the ``versions`` directory, each revision
carrying its own monotonic number and checksum. Revision files are never
rewritten; a new revision only appears by an atomic rename of a fully
synced file and its number is one greater than the previous newest, so
readers see a total order and old revisions are pruned once more than
``max_versions`` complete revisions exist. A crash or an interrupted
commit can therefore only ever leave complete revisions, and any reader
observes either the previous complete revision or the next one, never a
half-written schema. A revision is
parsed, structurally validated and checksummed completely before any of
its content is handed out; a missing or corrupt requested revision raises
``SchemaConflict`` and leaves every other revision usable.

``check`` and ``schema`` can either target an explicit revision number or
read the snapshot the lens was opened (``load``-ed) at; inference keeps
appending batches as before. ``versions`` lists the committed revisions
oldest first and ``rollback`` expresses the target revision's schema as a
brand new commit, so history is appended to and never rewritten. A
revision that has already been pruned (or never existed) makes a rollback
raise ``SchemaConflict`` without touching any committed revision.

A lens directory holding only the old single-file format (``schema.json``)
is still read; the legacy file is migrated in place into the revisions
layout on first read, and a failed migration leaves the original file and
the in-memory schema untouched and raises ``SchemaConflict`` so it can be
retried later.

The oldest segment of the history can be compacted into one baseline
version. A baseline file carries the schema and statistics exactly as they
stood at the end of the merged range (the folded tree is checked
field-for-field against the last merged revision before the switch), and a
small manifest in the versions directory is the single pointer naming at
most one baseline file. Compaction stages a temp artifact, validates it
fully, only then atomically replaces the manifest, and deletes no merged
input until that switch has landed; a crash mid-compaction is reconciled
into "completely happened" or "never happened" the next time the lock is
taken. Reads never wait on a compaction: while it runs they route through
the old manifest to complete revisions, and afterwards the baseline is
readable as its anchor revision while the revisions merged into it answer
``SchemaConflict``.

``compat(old, new)`` reads two committed snapshots without changing memory
or any revision and reports how the evolution between them affects the
records each side accepts. One symmetric tree diff derives both directions
at once, judged by the same rules ``check`` enforces: ``backward`` says
whether the new revision still accepts records legal under the old one,
``forward`` the reverse. Adding an optional field, relaxing a required
field or widening a type set is non-breaking in the direction that accepts;
removing a field, tightening optionality, narrowing a type set or dropping
a nested type branch is breaking there. A branch either side only describes
approximately (an overflow entry, an approximate field entry, or a
depth-capped subtree) cannot be settled and makes both directions
``unknown``, listing its source in ``unknown_reasons`` with the same paths
``stats`` uses; a revision compared with itself is compatible in both
directions with no changes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import copy
import hashlib
import itertools
import json
import os
import threading
import time

from typing import Any, Iterable, Iterator

except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - Windows

SCHEMA_FILENAME = "schema.json"
LOCK_FILENAME = "schema.lock"

REVISION_PREFIX = "revision-"
REVISION_SUFFIX = ".json"

# Version 1 files predate approximation markers; version 2 is the single
# file layout. All three encodings carry the same node tree, so legacy
# files migrate to the revisions layout without re-interpreting the tree.

# The overflow entry marks approximated locations in stats paths. It is a
# key no JSON object can literally carry, so it can never collide with a
# real field name (a field literally named "*" stays locatable as
# ``$["*"]`` while the marker renders as ``$.*``).
